notes: ACCESS: robots.txt (fetched 200 via curl_cffi) names no anthropic-ai/ClaudeBot/Claude-Web agent, so no Claude-specific disallow. As in the prior Home-Decor pass, HTML content routes serve the ISTL JS interstitial to curl, but sitemaps are unprotected and WebFetch renders past the interstitial; all counts here come from WebFetch reading the site's own rendered 'N items' header. TREE: https://www.nordstrom.com/navigation-sitemap.xml (200, 319KB) gives the complete nav tree - 2503 URLs sitewide, 73 of them under /browse/home. Grepping all 2503 nav URLs for furniture slugs (furniture|sofa|chair|table|bed|desk|cabinet|wardrobe|stool|bench|dresser|shelv|bookcase|seating|nightstand|armchair|ottoman|patio|outdoor) returns exactly ONE furniture browse node in the Home department: /browse/home/decor/furniture ('Accent Furniture'). Cross-checked against top-5k-browse-sitemap.xml (5005 URLs) - same result, no additional furniture nodes. The rendered Home mega-menu (WebFetch on /browse/home) also lists no Furniture/Seating/Tables/Chairs/Desks/Cabinets department. DEPTH: the Accent Furniture page's own left nav lists only siblings (All Home Decor, Art Prints & Wall Decor, Books/Games & Puzzles, Candles & Diffusers, Clocks, Decorative Accents, Decorative Pillows, Desk Accessories & Stationery, Jewelry Boxes & Holders, Lighting & Lamps, Mirrors, Picture Frames, Rugs, Storage & Organization, Throw Blankets, Vases & Planters) - no children under Accent Furniture. I also scanned all 23 navigation-filter-sitemap-*.xml files (~226k URLs; files 24+ return 403 and do not exist): the only filter URLs under /browse/home/decor/furniture are ?filterByBrand=... brand pages, i.e. the site publishes no product-type sub-facets for furniture. So Accent Furniture is a genuine leaf, recorded as such. QTY + SANITY CHECKS: header read three times - '493 items' on the canonical URL, '493 items' on ?page=1, '494 items' on ?page=7 (a +/-1 intra-session drift; flagged). Took 493. Pagination check: highest page number is 7 and ?page=8 renders an empty grid ('Looks like we don't have exactly what you're looking for'), which bounds the true total at 433-504 at the site's 72-per-page size established in the prior pass (ceil(493/72)=7) - consistent. The number is category-specific, not a site-wide constant (Outdoor Living reads 1986, Storage & Organization 839, on the same session). H1 confirmed as 'Accent Furniture' on every read. CONTENT CHECK: first 12 tiles are accent/console/side/drink tables, accent and bar stools - 11 of 12 are furniture (the 12th is a patio umbrella), so the node's primary product type is furniture. EXCLUDED AND WHY: 'Outdoor Living' (/browse/home/outdoor, 1986 items) - not a furniture node: its left rail is filter facets (Gender, Size, Color, Brand, Price, Fabric Care), not sub-categories, and its first 15 tiles are rugs, a BBQ grill, a fountain, a tray, a birdfeeder, a Dutch oven, lanterns, a tumbler, a speaker, a frog statue and a garden stake - one accent table among them. It is a cross-department seasonal roll-up, and its furniture stock already sits inside Accent Furniture (indoor/outdoor accent tables appear on page 1 of both). 'Storage & Organization' (839) excluded as standalone storage goods per the brief's storage-vs-furniture line - first 20 tiles are jewelry boxes, organizers, laundry baskets, hooks, drying racks and cable boxes, with only 3 furniture-type items (a wall-mounted bookcase, a floating nightstand, a freestanding bathroom cabinet); primary product type is storage goods, not furniture. 'Desk Accessories & Stationery' is stationery, not desks. Bedding, Bath, Rugs, Decorative Pillows, Table Linens, Mirrors, Lighting, Clocks, Wall Decor, Vases, Candles, Kitchenware, Dining & Entertainment, Electronics, Luggage & Travel, Pantry, Pet Accessories, Dorm Room Essentials, Fall Harvest and Halloween Decor are all out of furniture scope. OUT OF ASSIGNED SCOPE: the Kids department carries /browse/kids/baby-gear/highchairs (a chair by product type) and no crib/nursery-furniture node at all; my assignment scopes me to the Home department, and Nordstrom files highchairs under Baby Gear > Feeding, not under Home, so it is not recorded here. Noted in case the orchestrator wants it. Nordstrom is an apparel-led department store; a single 493-item accent-furniture node is the whole of its furniture catalogue.
